news.originalContent:
Several key races on Tuesday will determine if Republicans were able to beat expectations after trailing Democrats in the polls.

The elections appeared grim for Republicans in both the House and Senate races, particularly as voters remained dissatisfied with President Donald Trump’s handling of the economy. The races in deep-red states and districts, such as Ohio, Kansas and Texas, as well as in battleground states like Michigan, will be the most anticipated matchups to watch Tuesday night.

The Alaska Senate race has been embroiled in legal woes and investigations after The New York Times reported that former Democratic Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola’s campaign and aides with the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) coordinated to recruit other Republican candidates to run against Republican Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan. Former schoolteacher Dan J. Sullivan entered the race in June and will appear on the ballot, which could confuse voters into voting for the wrong Sullivan.

Aides with the DSCC introduced Democratic operative Jerid Kurtz to former members of Peltola’s team, who informed them he was in contact with another Sullivan from Petersburg. He attempted to recruit other Alaskans to run as Republicans by traveling to several communities and meeting different individuals in casual settings. (RELATED: Secret Scheme To Sabotage GOP Senator Revealed After Democrat Denied Involvement: REPORT)

Matthew Salisbury of Anchorage told the Times that he got a call from an unfamiliar number with an Ohio area code. The person, who identified himself as Zane, met with him at a pub and urged him to run for Senate. When the Times showed Salisbury a photograph of Kurtz, Salisbury confirmed that Kurtz was the person in question.

Alaska’s open voting system made this scheme possible, given that candidates can claim any party affiliation on the ballot without being vetted by parties themselves, according to the Times. Republicans backed an effort to help a candite serving time in a New York prison stay on the ballot when Peltola ran for reelection to the House in 2024.

The Department of Justice subpoenaed over three dozen individuals as part of its investigation into the Democrats’ scheme. Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether the scheme violated any laws.

Today’s New York Times reporting reveals disturbing new evidence of an organized effort to manipulate Alaska’s elections by recruiting candidates—including one with the same name as an incumbent U.S. Senator—to deliberately confuse voters and misdirect their votes. The Alaska Division of Elections investigated these very concerns in June of this year. The new reporting substantially supports the Division’s findings. I am therefore directing the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether this scheme violated Alaska’s laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted. The evidence will determine what happens next. Alaskans have a fundamental right to vote for the candidate they actually intend to support. Deliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections. Anyone or any organization found to have broken the law must be held accountable.

Peltola led by an average of 1.2 points as of Friday, though it remains to be seen how the Times’ report will impact her chances.

The other Sullivan’s candidacy prompted legal action to be taken over the summer. Division of Elections Director Carol Beecher informed Sullivan in an Aug. 26 letter that his declaration of candidacy “was not filed in order to declare an actual good-faith candidacy,” but rather to confuse voters into voting for the wrong Sullivan. After Sullivan appealed the ruling, Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews ruled he could remain on the ballot for the state’s primary.

The Alaska Supreme Court overturned that ruling in a June 30 decision and allowed the other Sullivan to be on the ballot. The DSCC and Peltola’s campaign celebrated the high court’s decision, according to the Times.

The other Sullivan changed his party affiliation from Republican to unaffiliated on Wednesday.

Democratic strategist Amber Lee authored a press release announcing the other Sullivan’s candidacy, metadata reviewed by the DCNF showed. Lee told The Hill in January that she believed there was a good chance Peltola could defeat Sullivan and previously hoped Peltola would run for governor.

Former public health official Abdul El-Sayed and former Republican Michigan Rep. Mike Rogers face a tight competition to replace Democratic Michigan Sen. Gary Peters. El-Sayed, a political newcomer who ran as the anti-establishment candidate, defeated Democratic Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens by one point in the Democratic primary after receiving endorsements from independent Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders, Democratic New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Democratic Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib.

The race will determine whether an anti-establishment Democrat can defeat an establishment, traditional Republican in a battleground state that President Donald Trump won by one point in 2024. El-Sayed would have to win over enough non-college educated, non-white and lower income voters to win, although he struggled with these voters during August’s Democratic primary.

Stevens won more than 50% of the vote in counties where less than 30% had a college education, while El-Sayed won nearly 60% of the vote in counties where at least 30% of residents held a bachelor’s degree, according to Politico. He also won in areas with universities while further-left candidates performed well with young voters and underperformed with black voters.

The Michigan Democrat held a 3.2-point lead against Rogers as of Friday, according to RealClearPolling. El-Sayed centered his campaign around affordability, fighting corporate money in politics and opposing the political establishment. He also supported cutting off aid to Israel and condemned the Iran war.

Rogers received an endorsement from Trump, although he broke with Trump during the general election cycle on the Iran war and Canadian tariffs. Rogers’ campaign released an advertisement on Oct. 8 that called for an end to a “tariff war” with Canada to help lower prices for consumers in the state, given that the state’s economy is strongly tied to the neighboring country.

Trump announced in July that 50% tariffs would be imposed on various Canadian goods, including wood and large motorcycles, under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, to force trade concessions. He implemented bans on specific Canadian alcohol, dairy and motorcycle products that went into effect on Sept. 29.

Rogers backed the tariffs in an Aug. 29 statement, stating they were “necessary” for Michigan’s economy.

“President Trump is right to put America First - and tariffs are necessary, but are not a size-fits-all solution,” Rogers said. “Elissa Slotkin and Gary Peters are missing in action. Michigan deserves a Senator who will work with President Trump to broker a trade deal with Canada that supports our farmers and gets the best deal for Michigan autoworkers and manufacturers.”

Rogers flip-flopped on the Iran war, stating in a Sept. 21 ad that it needed to end to bring costs down. He previously described Iran as an “imminent threat” and called U.S. military action a “win-win-win” for the nation.

Democratic voters largely voted out establishment incumbents and replaced them with further-left candidates, such as El-Sayed. Many in the Democratic coalition have increasingly become opposed to aiding Israel, which appeared evident when over 100 Democratic representatives voted for Republican Kentucky Rep. Thomas Massie’s amendment that would have slashed $3.3 billion in foreign aid to Israel.

The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) spent $30.6 million during the primary season, spending over $20 million opposing El-Sayed and over $10 million supporting Stevens, according to Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings. Rogers’ allies told AIPAC in August not to advertise on his behalf after El-Sayed won, although he said during an Oct. 9 debate that he welcomed support from AIPAC and anyone else who wanted to help his campaign.

AIPAC reportedly planned to give up to $9 million to a pro-Rogers super PAC, the Great Lakes Conservative Fund, in late October, anonymous sources told The New York Times. The spending was deliberately timed for after the Oct. 14 deadline so it would not appear on FEC filings before Election Day.

Current FEC filings do not show any contribution from AIPAC or UDP going to Rogers’ super PAC. UDP spent $95,000 on mailers to oppose El-Sayed on Oct. 9.

The race between Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic Texas state Rep. James Talarico remains tight, despite Texas being a traditionally red state.

Republicans spent over $300 million to help Paxton defeat Talarico. Texas has not had a Democratic senator since 1993, and Republicans control the state Legislature, attorney general’s and governor’s offices.

Talarico led Paxton by an average of 1.8 points as of Friday, according to RealClearPolling. The tight race has made Democrats hopeful they could flip a Senate seat blue for the first time in over three decades, prompting them to spend over $130 million in ad spending.

Corruption became a top issue for voters in the final stretch before the election, which likely hurt Paxton’s candidacy. The Republican-controlled Texas state Legislature impeached Paxton in 2023 on bribery and abuse of power charges, although the state Senate acquitted him.

Paxton was accused of misusing the office of the attorney general to protect and assist Austin real estate developer and political donor Nate Paul, who faced federal investigations. He allegedly intervened in lawsuits, issued favorable legal opinions to protect Paul’s properties from foreclosure and hired a special prosecutor to investigate claims helpful to Paul.

Paul allegedly paid for expensive renovations to Paxton’s home and employed a woman with whom Paxton had an extramarital affair. Paxton denied all wrongdoing.

Talarico repeatedly accused Paxton of being a corrupt politician who has used his power to get richer. Paxton’s net worth rose from $174,000 when he first entered the state Legislature in 2003 to an estimated $13 million currently, according to Forbes.

An October University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll found voters trusted Talarico more on handling corruption than Paxton by ten percentage points.

Talarico stated in 2021 that God was “non-binary” and that transgender children were made in His image. He claimed that the biblical account of Jesus’ conception justified abortion and also said on a May 2023 podcast that he loved transgender kids when asked to name something he loved other than his family and friends.

Paxton argued on the campaign trail that Talarico is too liberal for Texas.

The Texas Democrat left the campaign trail for nine days during the first week of October, claiming he had a “nasty case of the flu.”

Paxton defeated Republican Texas Sen. John Cornyn by a 28-point margin in May after Trump endorsed him last-minute. During the Republican primary, Republican Texas Sen. John Cornyn and his allies referred to Paxton as “Crooked Ken” and called him “corrupt to the core” in one ad. Talarico and his allies released attack ads calling out Paxton’s alleged corruption.

Ohio Senate & Governor’s races

Democrats are eyeing Ohio as a potential win against Republicans, who control the state Legislature and governor’s office. Former Democratic Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown and Democratic Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton held slight leads in the polls against Republican Ohio Sen. Jon Husted and Republican Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy.

Brown led Husted by an average of 2.6 points, according to RealClearPolling. Trump won Ohio by a twelve-point margin, 55.2% to 43.9%. Husted assumed office in January 2025 to replace Vice President J.D. Vance.

Acton led Ramaswamy by an average of 4.3 points as of Friday, according to RealClearPolling. Ramaswamy faced backlash after an advertisement featuring Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, telling voters not to vote for her.

Acton and her mother have been estranged since 1978, when she was 12 years old. She and her younger brother were removed from Arthur’s custody after her husband was charged with sexually abusing Acton.

Ramaswamy’s poll numbers dropped six points Thursday after the ad aired, according to Truthout.

Republican Maine Sen. Susan Collins faces a tough challenge against Democratic Maine Senate candidate Troy Jackson, who entered the race late in the game. Heating fuel prices became a top issue for Maine voters since the Iran war began, which could give Democrats an advantage in the deep blue state.

Jackson held a slight lead over Collins in the deep-blue state, holding a 1.4 point average lead, according to RealClearPolling. Former Vice President Kamala Harris won Maine by a 52.4% to 45.5% margin in the 2024 election. Maine Democrats control the governor’s office, attorney general’s office and the state Legislature.

Despite Maine being a blue state, Collins has won five Senate races since 1996.

The two candidates both campaigned on the high cost of living, particularly the high-heating costs in Maine. The average statewide heating fuel prices rose to $6.05 per gallon as of Oct. 26. Roughly half of the population in Maine rely on heating oil as their principal energy source in the winter, meaning they could face an increase of thousands of dollars in heating.

The Iran war caused heating fuel prices to soar, given that the Strait of Hormuz handles roughly 20% to 25% of the world’s seaborne oil and petroleum product flow. Collins voted to extend U.S. military operations in Iran five times since February.

Collins and independent Maine Sen. Angus King urged the Trump administration to tap into the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve to help lower costs before the elections. She joined a bipartisan push to expedite the release of over $38 million in federal home heating assistance for Maine households.

Collins initially ran against former Democratic Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner, who dropped out of the race after a woman accused him of rape.

Republican Kansas Sen. Roger Marshall is trailing Democratic Kansas Senate nominee Adam Hamilton by an average of 2.6 points. A Democratic victory would be a major upset, given that Kansas has not had a Democratic senator since 1939.

The Republican senator sued 700 of his patients for outstanding debts during his time as an OB-GYN, which led to 81 arrests, The New York Times reported. Some facing lawsuits were mothers with outstanding bills from their deliveries, and many patients lacked insurance. One mother had a nine-month-old baby when her bank account was garnished.

Marshall paid a bakery $1,300 after its owner, Holly Thomas, accused his 2020 campaign of leaving a nearly $700 bill unpaid for six years. The senator said on X that he paid the bill and apologized to the bakery, claiming he had “no idea” how the bill went unpaid for six years.

RealClearPolling averages showed Marshall and Hamilton in a tie in mid-October.

The close race caused the Senate Leadership Fund, Senate Republicans’ campaign arm, to spend $14 million to support Marshall.

The Senate Majority PAC, the Democrats’ Senate campaign arm, launched a $5 million statewide television advertising campaign that plans to run through Election Day, indicating that Democrats were increasingly confident they could flip the seat, Politico reported. One ad attacked Marshall for voting against an amendment that would require the Department of Justice (DOJ) to release the files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The PAC’s research found that Epstein ads can sway elections three to six points in the Democrats’ direction.

The economy remained a top issue for Kansas voters, according to an Emerson College poll from Thursday. Diesel prices averaged $6.03 per gallon in Kansas, which Marshall largely attributed to the war in Ukraine. Hamilton pinned the high Diesel prices on Trump and the Iran war, which has likely resonated with farmers across the state.

Elections forecasters projected that Democrats would retake the House in the next Congress. Republicans redrew several districts to give themselves an advantage in November, but many Republican-held seats are still at risk of flipping for Democrats.

Republicans hoped to flip Democratic Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz’s seat in Florida’s 25th district. The state redrew the district with hopes that a Republican could pick up the seat, although Cook Political Report moved the race from the “Toss Up” column to “Lean Democratic.”

The Congressional Leadership Fund, the top House super PAC, slashed $6 million in ad spending in the district to oppose Moskowitz, who is running against former Republican Boca Raton Mayor Scott Singer. The No Going Back PAC, a super PAC backed by MAGA Inc., planned to spend $6.3 million in the district.

The super PAC also slashed $3 million from Texas’ 28th district, which was redrawn to help Republicans oust Democratic Texas Rep. Henry Cuellar. Trump won the district by seven percentage points in 2024.

Cook Political Report shifted the races in Arizona’s sixth district, Colorado’s eighth district, Virginia’s second district and Wisconsin’s third district into the “Lean Democratic” column less than two weeks before Election Day. Republican Reps. Juan Ciscomani of Arizona, Gabe Evans of Colorado, Jen Kiggans of Virginia and Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin currently hold those seats.

Eight Republican-held seats shifted in Democrats’ favor, including Republican Pennsylvania Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick’s seat in Pennsylvania’s first district and Republican Indiana Rep. Victoria Spartz’s seat in Indiana’s fifth district, according to Cook Political Report. The projection would give Democrats up to 240 seats in the House in the next Congress if they flip between 12 and 25 seats.

Republican Ohio Rep. Max Miller could lose to Democratic Ohio congressional nominee Brian Poindexter in Ohio’s 7th district, where Trump won by 10.6 percentage points in 2024. Miller’s ex-wife, Emily Moreno, accused him of domestic abuse, which Miller repeatedly denied.

Miller refused to drop out of the race when some in his party called on him to drop out. Among those who called on him to drop out included Husted and Miller’s ex-father-in-law, Republican Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno. Miller did not exit the race by the necessary deadline for Ohio’s Republican party to replace him, meaning Poindexter would have remained uncontested if Miller had exited the race.

Poindexter out-raised Miller by a wide margin in the third quarter. The Democrat reported $2.47 million in receipts and $1.72 million in spending between July 1 and September 30, while Miller raised $1.14 million and ended September with about $944,000 on hand.

Republican New York Rep. Mike Lawler faces a competitive reelection bid against Democratic New York congressional nominee Cait Conley in New York’s 17th district. He is one of the most vulnerable Republican incumbents since Harris won his district in the 2024 election by less than one point, although former President Joe Biden won it by ten points in 2020.

The candidates were neck-and-neck as of Friday. A McLaughlin & Associates survey from late September showed Lawler leading by three points, while an Emerson College poll showed Conley leading by two points.

Lawler painted Conley as a radical socialist on the campaign trail, while Conley tied Lawler to Trump. The district is one of the most centrist in the U.S.

Democratic New York Rep. Tom Suozzi is defending his seat in New York’s third district against former Republican New York state Assemblyman Michael LiPetri. Suozzi, who replaced former Republican New York Rep. George Santos after he was expelled from Congress, narrowly won his seat in 2024 by a three-point margin. The No Going Back PAC, a super PAC tied to Trump’s political organization MAGA Inc., spent nearly $8 million to support LiPetri, which included $5.7 million in ad spending to attack Suozzi.

Republican New York congressional nominee Anthony Constantino and Democratic New York congressional nominee Blake Gendebien are running for an open seat in New York’s 21st district after Republican New York Rep. Elise Stefanik decided not to run. While traditionally a Republican district, the candidates are neck-and-neck while tariffs, the economy and relations with Canada remained top issues.

A Public Policy Polling survey from mid-October found Constantino leading by two points, while a New York Times/Siena College poll showed Gendebien leading by four points.

Republican Pennsylvania Rep. Rob Bresnahan is defending his seat against Democratic Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti in Pennsylvania’s 8th district. The cost of living remained the top issue in the district, prompting Bresnahan to call on the Iran war to come to an immediate end. About two-thirds of Americans disapprove of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, which is expected to cost many Republicans House seats.

An Emerson College poll showed Cognetti leading 52% to 48%, while A New York Times, Philadelphia Inquirer and Siena University poll found her ahead by a 51% to 46% margin.

Republican Michigan Rep. Tom Barrett is facing off with Democratic Michigan congressional nominee William Lawrence, a further-left political activist, in Michigan’s seventh district. Lawrence co-founded the Sunrise Movement, an organization that advocates for action on climate change.

Recent polls showed Lawrence leading Barrett, including an Emerson College poll where Lawrence led by eight points.
news.content: چندین رقابت کلیدی در روز سه‌شنبه تعیین خواهد کرد که آیا جمهوری‌خواهان پس از عقب افتادن از دموکرات‌ها در نظرسنجی‌ها می‌توانند انتظارات را پشت سر بگذارند یا خیر. این انتخابات برای جمهوری‌خواهان در هر دو رقابت مجلس نمایندگان و سنا تاسف‌بار به نظر می‌رسد، به‌ویژه که رای‌دهندگان همچنان از عملکرد دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در اقتصاد ناراضی بودند. رقابت‌ها در ایالت‌ها و مناطق با رنگ قرمز عمیق، مانند اوهایو، کانزاس و تگزاس، و همچنین در ایالت‌های میدان نبرد مانند میشیگان، مورد انتظارترین مسابقات برای تماشای سه‌شنبه شب خواهند بود. پس از گزارش نیویورک تایمز که نماینده سابق دموکرات آلاسکا، نماینده سابق دموکرات آلاسکا، مسابقه سنای آلاسکا درگیر مشکلات و تحقیقات قانونی شده است. کمپین مری پلتولا و دستیاران کمیته مبارزات انتخاباتی سناتورهای دموکرات (DSCC) برای جذب سایر نامزدهای جمهوری خواه برای رقابت در برابر دن سالیوان، سناتور جمهوری خواه آلاسکا، هماهنگ شدند. دان جی. سالیوان، معلم سابق مدرسه در ماه ژوئن وارد رقابت شد و در برگه رای ظاهر خواهد شد، که می تواند رای دهندگان را در رای دادن به سالیوان اشتباه گیج کند. دستیاران DSCC، جرید کورتز، عامل دموکرات را به اعضای سابق تیم پلتولا معرفی کردند، که به آنها اطلاع دادند که با سالیوان دیگری از پترزبورگ در تماس است. او سعی کرد با سفر به چندین جامعه و ملاقات با افراد مختلف در محیط‌های معمولی، سایر آلاسکاها را برای نامزدی جمهوری‌خواهان استخدام کند. (مرتبط: طرح مخفی خرابکاری سناتور جمهوری خواه پس از رد دخالت دموکرات ها فاش شد: گزارش) متیو سالزبری از انکوریج به تایمز گفت که از یک ناشناس با او تماس گرفته است

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.
news.content: ارتش اسرائیل به حملاتی که شب گذشته در جنوب لبنان از جمله در روستای کفرمان انجام شد، پرداخت و گفت که این حملات بعد از ظهر دوشنبه پس از پرتاب دو پهپاد انفجاری توسط تروریست‌های حزب‌الله به سمت نیروهای اسرائیلی در خط الراس علی طاهر در جنوب لبنان آغاز شد. هیچ نیروی ارتش اسرائیل در پرتاب هواپیماهای بدون سرنشین آسیبی ندید و ارتش اعلام کرد که بلافاصله حمله به زیرساخت‌های حزب‌الله را در چندین منطقه در جنوب لبنان از جمله تأسیسات ذخیره‌سازی سلاح آغاز کرده است.   هیچ نیروی ارتش اسرائیل در پرتاب هواپیماهای بدون سرنشین آسیبی ندید و ارتش اعلام کرد که بلافاصله حمله به زیرساخت‌های حزب‌الله را در چندین منطقه در جنوب لبنان از جمله تأسیسات ذخیره‌سازی سلاح آغاز کرده است. خودرویی که در آن دو نفر کشته شدند. آسوشیتدپرس گزارش داد که این خودرو متعلق به انجمن پیشاهنگی و نجات لبنان، الرساله است و یکی از کشته شدگان، امدادگر این سازمان است. دو نفر دیگر زخمی شدند. همزمان، گزارش‌های لبنانی حاکی از آن است که ساختمانی در کفارمان که تعداد زیادی از مردم در آن اقامت داشتند نیز مورد اصابت قرار گرفت و 9 نفر از جمله زن و کودک کشته و 11 نفر زخمی شدند.   ارتش اسرائیل در پاسخ گفت: قبل از حملات، اقداماتی برای کاهش آسیب به افراد غیرمجاز از جمله استفاده از مهمات دقیق و نظارت هوایی انجام شد. این ادعا که در نتیجه این اعتصابات به چند نفر آسیب وارد شده است، در حال بررسی است. ارتش اسرائیل گفت که علاوه بر این، دنبال کنید

news.originalContent:
از اواسط دهه ۱۳۹۰ نرخ تورم در ایران سیر صعودی گرفته و بویژه قیمت مواد غذایی با سرعتی بیشتر از سایر کالاها و خدمات مصرفی افزایش یافته است.

همین است که بسیاری احساس می‌کنند نرخ رسمی تورم با تجربه آن‌ها از افزایش قیمت‌ها، مخصوصا موقع خرید هفتگی خواروبار همخوانی ندارد.

محاسبه‌گر تورم مواد غذایی به شما اجازه می‌دهد که با انتخاب محتویات سبد خرید ماهانه‌تان ببینید هزینه سبد شما چقدر نسبت به یک سال پیش بالا رفته و نرخ تورمی که برای خرید این اقلام  تجربه می‌کنید، چقدر است.

مرکز آمار ایران در گزارشی که ۶ آبان ۱۴۰۵ منتشر کرد، نرخ تورم یک سال منتهی به مهر را ۷۶٫۸ درصد اعلام کرد.

در گزارش این نهاد نرخ تورم نقطه به نقطه در مهرماه امسال ۸۸٫۷ درصد اعلام شده است به این معنی که خانوارهای ایرانی، در شهریور امسال در مقایسه با شهریور پارسال برای خرید مجموعه کالاها و خدمات یکسان حدود ۹۰ درصد بیشتر باید می‌پرداختند.

سبد خرید ماهانه مواد غذایی شما:میزان خرید ماهانه این مواد غذایی را وارد کنید تا ببینید هزینه‌های شما چند تومان و چند درصد تغییر کرده است.

سبد خرید شما خالی است. لطفا چند مورد از لیست بالا انتخاب کنید.

این محاسبات بر اساس آمارهای رسمی از متوسط قیمت مواد غذایی در مناطق شهری ایران انجام می‌شود. محاسبه‌گر، هزینه سبد انتخابی شما را طبق قیمت‌هایی تازه‌ترین ماهی که داده‌های آن به صورت عمومی منتشر شده، محاسبه می‌کند و آن را با متوسط هزینه آن در ماه مشابه یک سال و پنج سال قبل مقایسه می‌‌کند و از روی آن نرخ تورم سالانه و نیز میزان افزایش درازمدت هزینه آن را محاسبه می‌کند.

* حریم خصوصی شما برای استفاده از این محاسبه‌گر محفوظ است. بی‌بی‌سی اطلاعاتی را که شما در این محاسبه‌گر وارد می‌کنید، جمع‌آوری نمی‌کند و به آن‌ها دسترسی ندارد.

news.originalContent: Senior government officials admit that Israel's public opinion in the international community "has never been worse." According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten.  Follow Ynetnews on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | TikTok >> More stories: IDF releases name of fallen soldier in West Bank terror attack UN chief in Rafah crossing says world 'seen enough' of Gaza war Two Air Force pilots reminisce about their murdered brothers: 'There's no room for pain in the air' The officials added that the intensity of accusations made against Israel only increases, and attempts to equate Hamas's actions in Israel are being made, with allegations accusing IDF soldiers of sexually harassing Palestinian prisoners. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

news.originalContent: Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guards warned anti-government protesters of "decisive" action if unrest over gasoline price hikes do not cease, state television reported on Monday. The warning appeared to hint at a looming crackdown on protests that flared nationwide in response to an official announcement on Friday of gasoline rationing and price hikes of at least 50 percent. "If necessary we will take decisive and revolutionary action against any continued moves to disturb the people's peace and security," the Guards said in a statement carried by state media.
news.content: تلویزیون دولتی روز دوشنبه گزارش داد که سپاه پاسداران قدرتمند ایران به معترضان ضد دولتی هشدار داد که اگر ناآرامی ها بر سر افزایش قیمت بنزین متوقف نشود، اقدام «قاطعانه» خواهند کرد. به نظر می‌رسد این هشدار به سرکوب اعتراض‌هایی که در سراسر کشور در واکنش به اعلام رسمی روز جمعه مبنی بر سهمیه‌بندی بنزین و افزایش حداقل 50 درصدی قیمت‌ها شعله‌ور شد، اشاره می‌کند. سپاه پاسداران در بیانیه‌ای که توسط رسانه‌های دولتی منتشر شد، گفت: «در صورت لزوم، در برابر هرگونه اقدام مستمر برای برهم زدن آرامش و امنیت مردم، اقدام قاطع و انقلابی خواهیم کرد».
